intro: A network head may require a fixed grid even when input images differ in size. Adaptive pooling chooses averaging regions from the requested output dimensions.
task: Average the documented floor-to-ceil regions for every output location.
requirements: image is a height-by-width matrix and output_size has two integer entries in 1..64.

For output row i, use input rows floor(i*H/OH) through ceil((i+1)*H/OH)-1; use the analogous interval for columns. Return each rectangular region’s mean. Regions may overlap, and output dimensions may exceed input dimensions.

Use finite real numeric values of magnitude at most 1e6, excluding boolean inputs. Each array axis has 1..64 entries and at most 65536 elements total unless a stricter bound is stated. Return NumPy arrays for array outputs, preserve caller inputs, and raise ValueError for invalid inputs.

hints.title: Follow the data
hints.body: Compute bin boundaries from the ratio of input length to output length.

hints.title: Check the boundary
hints.body: Use a ceiling for the right boundary to ensure every region contains at least one source element.

explanation: Adaptive pooling summarizes variable input sizes with a fixed output shape. Floor and ceiling boundaries can create overlapping bins when dimensions do not divide evenly.
The result is an average over each region rather than a resampled value at one coordinate. Consequently it behaves differently from bilinear interpolation and from disjoint block pooling.
